The '''Donegall Lecturership at Trinity College Dublin''' is one of two endowed mathematics positions at [[Trinity College Dublin]] (TCD), the other being the [[Erasmus Smith's Chair of Mathematics]]. The Donegall (sometimes spelt Donegal) Lectureship was endowed in 1668 by [[Arthur Chichester, 3rd Earl of Donegall|the 3rd Earl of Donegall]].<ref name=calendar>[https://books.google.com/books?id=3-UNAAAAQAAJ&dq=Donegal+Lectures+of+Mathematics&pg=PA136 The Dublin University Calendar 1877]</ref><ref>[https://www.maths.tcd.ie/about/400Hist/4.php  Mathematics at TCD: The eighteenth century] 400 years of mathematics by [[T. D. Spearman]]</ref> In 1675, after the [[Stuart Restoration|restoration]], it was combined with the previous public Professor in Mathematics position that had been created in 1652 by the Commonwealth parliament. 

For much of its history, the Donegall Lectureship was awarded to a [[mathematician]] as an additional honour which came with a supplementary income.<ref>[https://www.maths.tcd.ie/pub/ims/bull82/obit.pdf Obituary of Timothy Gayleard Murphy] Irish Math. Society Bulletin, No 82, Winter 2018, pp. 4–10</ref> Since 1967, the lectureship has been awarded to a leading international scientist who visits the Department of Pure and Applied Mathematics and gives talks, including a public lecture called the Donegall Lecture.
